questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That they offered courses on continental philosophy, which my home university doesn't! Also, the fact that it was in Germany as i had a wish, both academically and personally to learn German. my original plan was also to go with my, now, Ex-girlfriend and since it was an EU4+ Uni, there were enough spots in the exchange program for us both. that plan didn't materialize as we broke up, it was however a plus that there were more students from my home country as it helped me deal with bouts of longing for home.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: not that easy - not alot of information online and the systems that are in place are confusing... when however i realized that germany barely has begun its digitalization and that most things require that you show up in person or call at certain very limited office hours, it was easier to figure out if not to actually succeed with.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: a great buddy program, a couple of introductory days and some great student tutors - but not a lot of helpt from the Administration...

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: dont take the host accommodations - they are cheap but not of great quality and placed relatively far from the central parts of the city(though that is still pretty close, to be fair...). My friends who found accomodations for themselves had nicer accommodation, more interaction with native Germans and better opportunities for social and cultural activities.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: there is no real "on campus" for the humanities, the campus is spread all over the city. altstadt is however closest while weststadt and neuheim are the prettiest and offers the opportunity of avoiding the heavy touristic aspects of altstadt. however the suburbs are also pretty nice and reachable on bike or by tram.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: i received my matrikkelnr. too late to apply to certain courses. in several of the courses you had to write directly to the professor or show up at the start of classes in order to register. also several courses utilized two different online systems at the same time - i had to apply to both... examine registartion was pretty simple though

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: other students? my buddy and my tutors...

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: after much struggle i succeeded for the most part - the piont system was confusing though and i ended up taking too many courses...

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: get help from the student body, they know how shit works

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: the level was way higher than at my sending institution but i never felt like i couldn't follow - questions and discussion was highly encouraged and the educators very helpful. overall an A+ experience

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: better... smaller courses, both when it came to the amount of students and the amount of points, much more specialized and in-depth. lots of seminar work, not a lot of lecturing which encouraged that students worked with the material themselves.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Jaspers&Sartre
Phänomenologie und psychopathologie der Affektivität
Cost of Comfort
Wiederholung
Introduktion to philosophy

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
all of them! the courses change each semester though so it wont be possible...
Phäno&psycho is taught by the leading researcher in psychiatric phenomenology and is great!
the introduction to philosophy is a bit boring but really helpfull in order to get the terminology specific to the field in german!

questions.answer: some necessary insurances... the high price for internet

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: food were cheaper - cafés, restaurants and bars as well...accommodation was pretty cheap too

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: really hard to find practice rooms for music!!! the uni was no help and there seems to be almost no culture for musicians in Heidelberg... it was also not permitted to play in apartments owned by the university :(

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
sports...
a few classical concerts i guess
a litterature festival

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: go out a lot!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: go to cave54 on tuesdays for jazznight, boho for socializing on monday nights. hang on the neckarwiese when its sunny, and when really hot go to the tiergardenschwimbad. go on weekendtrips with the other Erasmus students and maybe go to bodensee or Tübingen or something

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: relatively easy!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: dont be afraid to ask if people want to drink a cup of coffee or weineschörle after class - people are more outgoing than in in denmark and the city is small enough that fresh blood from exchange students is fascinating to the local students!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: the supermarkets sucked... the bike lanes were nonexisting and traffic rules confusing

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the openness

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
its okay to be tired and say no! prioritizing both social, academic and recreational time is important
it is easier than you think to establish a network
have fun with it! everything will work out

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: ask questions if there is something you don't understand, it'll spare both you and your professors time, and most people are very understanding! confusion is normal when you arrive at a new place but it only goes away if you ask the questions

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: the social and cultural parts.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: the language barrier

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
